findings.statement: On real photographs of people the NSFWJS models put most of their probability on Drawing rather than Neutral, so the v1 confident-Neutral policy withheld almost every ordinary fashion photograph (91.5% of the 341 calibration photographs). The synthetic fabric fixtures Story 6.2 used scored Neutral near 1 and could not show this.
findings.crossCheck: Recorded once, 2026-10-16: 65 corpus photographs were also classified through the upstream nsfwjs.load("MobileNetV2Mid") classify path with the union @tensorflow/tfjs CPU backend, in a throwaway install outside this repository, and 62 of 65 reached the same disposition, so the effect is the model and the policy, not this repository’s preprocessing.
findings.consequence: Policy v2 was calibrated on the calibration half only: Neutral plus Drawing (NSFWJS’s safe-for-work classes) above a floor, with every unsafe bound, including the joint bound on Hentai, Porn and Sexy, held at its v1 value. The holdout half measures the result, and the gate is computed there.

findings.statement: On the 298 holdout photographs (split by creator) the policy withheld 9.1% (Wilson 95% upper bound 12.9%), against 16.7% on the 341 calibration photographs it was chosen on; 7 holdout photographs were blocked. The gate's ceiling is 5%, so it fails. The commonest cause is unsafe aggregate at or above its ceiling (17 of 27). Every withheld and blocked holdout photograph is listed with what it shows. Closing the gate needs a different model or a decision to loosen an unsafe bound, and neither was taken here.

The frozen text holdout, written after the allow list froze and never tuned against, withheld clean captions in 4 of 7 languages (es 1 of 420, fr 1 of 420, it 2 of 420, pt 4 of 420; by severity medium 3, high 1, low 4), where the in-sample clean half the allow list was built against withheld 0. The in-sample figure overstated the list quality; the holdout is the honest one. Fixing these means changing the lists or the allow list and then freezing a new holdout, because tuning against this one would turn it into a second tuning set.

The sweep, the corpora and the review found 5 defects in the Story 6.2 screening code, each fixed with a regression test: a duplicated class name could overwrite another class’s slot and publish (now class_mismatch); leet classing could create a doubled letter the index had already collapsed, so f r 3 5 s e published; a multi-word term cut at a different place, vai-tefoder, reached no matching pass; one allow-listed word disabled every multi-word term containing it; a re-split multi-word term written in leetspeak (k1ll yours elf) published, because the re-split pass compared plain letters only.

limitations.statement: Recall against real unsafe imagery is inherited from the upstream NSFWJS mobilenet_v2_mid model at nsfwjs@4.3.0 and is not measured in this repository. No unsafe imagery may enter it, so no corpus here establishes that the model emits a high Hentai or Porn probability for genuinely unsafe input.
limitations.residualRisk: An unsafe image that the model reads as safe for work (Drawing plus Neutral above 0.85, Hentai plus Porn below 0.1, Sexy below 0.15, all of them together below 0.15) publishes automatically, and how often that happens has not been measured here. Counting Drawing toward the safe mass, which the calibration chose, widens what publishes compared with the v1 Neutral-only floor; no unsafe bound, joint or single, is looser than v1.
limitations.mitigation: Automatic publication requires a confident safe-for-work reading with every unsafe bound at its v1 value, and every other outcome routes to a human, so a recall failure on uncertain input becomes review load rather than a published post. The report action (Story 6.4), the moderator queue (Story 6.10) and both rollout flags staying closed until the moderator rota is real cover the confident-miss case.
limitations.revisitWhen: A moderator confirms a published post that should have been withheld, the model or its version changes, or the beta cohort grows past what two moderators can watch reactively.

limitations.statement: The 7 term lists have pinned, attributable community provenance (LDNOOBW at one commit, CC-BY-4.0) and a repository-graded overlay, but no native-speaker review. LDNOOBW was compiled to keep words out of image-search autocomplete, which is broader than abuse screening, and the lists are uneven: en carries 403 upstream entries and de 66.
limitations.residualRisk: Abuse written with words outside the lists publishes; ordinary words the lists carry route captions to review, and the frozen text holdout measures how often that happens on copy nobody tuned against. Upstream-only entries are graded profanity at medium severity, so none of them blocks on its own.
limitations.mitigation: Every language runs against every submission, obfuscation families are normalised before matching, mixed scripts route to review, the repository allow list records why each exemption exists, and the clean-copy gate measures the false-positive cost per language on a holdout.
limitations.revisitWhen: A native-speaker reviewer is available for any of the seven languages, moderators report a missed term or a recurring false positive, or a new locale is enabled.

limitations.statement: Fashion term 'lolita' always goes to review. It names a fashion subculture and is also a child-sexualisation keyword, and on a 13+ product the policy keeps it as a deliberate review term rather than allow-listing it. The French 'baiser' is kept the same way: a kiss as a noun, the commonest vulgar verb otherwise.
limitations.residualRisk: Every Lolita-fashion caption and every caption using the French noun waits for a moderator, which delays those members and adds to review load.
limitations.mitigation: Both are recorded with their reasons in the policy (text.deliberateReviewTerms); startup refuses a policy that allow-lists or drops either; the corpora label the captions carrying them as expected review and report them beside the clean-copy gate; and a moderator clears an ordinary post in one action.
limitations.revisitWhen: Moderators find these captions are almost always cleared, or the platform raises its minimum age.

limitations.statement: The safe corpus is drawn from openly licensed stock and community photography on Openverse, filtered to fashion titles and tags. It may not match the distribution of what members actually upload: phone photos, mirror selfies, low light, partial bodies, swimwear.
limitations.residualRisk: The real review rate on member uploads may be higher than the measured rate, which would raise the moderators’ daily load above the projection.
limitations.mitigation: The corpus is split by creator and caps any creator at 5% of it, the projection is reported at the Wilson upper bound and across a range of volumes, and the moderator queue shows the actual rate from the first beta day.
limitations.revisitWhen: The first two weeks of beta traffic exist: replace the projection with the observed withheld rate and re-measure if it differs from the corpus rate by more than its interval.

limitations.statement: The beta operates with 2 moderators (ADR-013 staffing plan) covering a 24-hour review SLA through rotating shifts.
limitations.residualRisk: A spike in withheld posts, an incident-mode period where every submission routes to review, or one moderator’s absence can breach the SLA.
limitations.mitigation: Rollout flags open reading and writing separately, the daily posting cap bounds per-account volume, the projected review load is in this payload, and the SLA monitor (Story 6.12) alerts before a breach.
limitations.revisitWhen: The projected or observed daily review load exceeds what 2 people can clear inside the 24-hour SLA, or the cohort is widened.

limitations.statement: The hosted canary has run; runtime latency and memory are still from the local container under the sandbox resource limits, and the regression gate committed in the model manifest comes from developer hardware.
limitations.residualRisk: The hosted CPU may be slower or noisier than the emulation, and the regression gate does not yet describe production hardware.
limitations.mitigation: The latency and memory gates run on the emulated profile, the memory gate reads the real container’s cgroup peak at the largest accepted upload, and the hosted canary records real queue latency and screening duration.
limitations.revisitWhen: The worker is deployed: run the measurements inside the hosted container and re-baseline the regression gate from them.

limitations.statement: The production Upstash database is on Pay as You Go, which bills every command (0.20 USD per 100K). An idle BullMQ worker polls Redis continuously. With BullMQ defaults it measured 6,516 commands an hour, about 9.51 USD a month while idle; the worker now blocks for 300 seconds between idle polls and checks for stalled jobs every 120 seconds, and the measured idle cost plus projected traffic is in the Redis section. The worker uses the production Upstash database the API already uses for its own queues. These figures are the community worker alone; the API’s commands are billed on the same database.
limitations.residualRisk: The bill grows with every command, the API’s own commands are billed on the same database and are not in this measurement, and a volume past 881 posts a day takes the worker alone past 5 USD a month. A connection that dies silently during a long block delays pickup until the block times out.
limitations.mitigation: A new job wakes the blocked worker at once, so the long block costs no pickup latency; the outbox dispatcher and the stale-review sweep are the backstops for a dead connection; the deployment guide names the provider dashboard figures to watch after the first day (commands and cost, which count the API and the worker together).
limitations.revisitWhen: The Upstash console projects the database past 5 USD for a month, or daily submissions approach 881.

rollback.scope: The hosted community worker. The API, web and mobile surfaces are not deployed by this story.
steps: Leave community_read_enabled and community_write_enabled disabled; they are disabled now and nothing in this story changes them.

Redeploy the previous image on the host (Northflank keeps prior builds per commit), or stop the service. A stopped worker leaves queued jobs in Redis; they run when a worker returns, and the stale-review sweep moves anything pending too long to review_failed.

If the model itself is the problem, set COMMUNITY_NSFW_SCREENER=unavailable with COMMUNITY_NSFW_INCIDENT_MODE=unavailable and COMMUNITY_NSFW_INCIDENT_REFERENCE, and restart: every submission routes to human review and nothing auto-publishes.
Run the hosted canary after any rollback to confirm the restored worker publishes the safe fixture under a real-model identity, and that the worker name carries the commit you rolled back to.
Re-screen posts refused during the incident with the retained-job replay procedure in the deployment guide.

communityBetaGate.statement: A model-readiness signature is not a launch decision. Community Beta opens only when all eight gate signatures are recorded, and the rollout flags stay disabled until then.
